meta.source: New Zealand Law Style Guide, 3rd edition (2018)

types.name: Reported case (New Zealand)

components.label: Case name
components.formatting: Italicise including the 'v'; parties' names exactly as on the first page of the report; no full stops in abbreviations; where a party is a natural person omit given names and initials; cite only first plaintiff/appellant and first defendant/respondent (no '& Anor'/'& Ors'); use legal-status abbreviations (Ltd, Co, Inc, (in liq), (in rec), (in stat man), plc, Pty, Assoc, Corp); shorten 'In re'/'In the matter of' to 'Re'; do not abbreviate 'ex parte'; reported Crown cases keep name as in report
components.notes: 3.2.1. Common/abbreviated names may follow the citation in square brackets in footnotes.

components.label: Neutral citation
components.includedWhen: included when the case has an official neutral citation (SC 2005, CA 2007, HC 2012, etc.); depends on availability per 3.3.3
components.omittedWhen: omit for decisions predating adoption of neutral citation by that court/tribunal; never use unofficial NZLII-style numbers
components.formatting: form [year] COURT number per rule 3.3; separated from the reported citation by a comma

components.label: Year
components.formatting: square brackets [year] if the report is organised by year; round brackets (year) if organised by volume number; if heard one year and delivered another, use the year judgment was delivered

components.label: Volume number
components.includedWhen: included when the report is organised by volume, or when a year-organised report has more than one volume that year
components.omittedWhen: omit if a year-organised report has only one volume for the year
components.formatting: always Arabic numerals even if the report uses Roman numerals

components.label: Report series
components.formatting: abbreviate using the report's own abbreviation with unnecessary punctuation removed; overseas series number in round brackets after abbreviation e.g. DLR (4th); official series (NZLR) preferred over unofficial

components.label: Starting page
components.includedWhen: always (or case number for CCH-style series, prefixed by pilcrow ¶)
components.formatting: no 'page'/'p'/'pp'; give first page of the case even where a subsequent appeal starts later under the same headnote

components.label: Court identifier
components.includedWhen: included in round brackets when there is NO neutral citation
components.omittedWhen: omit when a neutral citation is present (court is evident from it); omit for single-court series (CLR, US, SCR)
components.formatting: abbreviation in round brackets e.g. (CA), (HC), (SC for pre-1980 Supreme Court); jurisdiction tag prefixed without space for multijurisdictional series e.g. (NZCA), (Fiji HC), (NZHC)

components.label: Pinpoint reference
components.formatting: paragraph numbers in square brackets [29] (no 'para'); page numbers plain (no 'p'); subparagraph [238(a)]; ranges with en dash no spaces; multiples separated by commas with final 'and'

types.bracketRules: Year in square brackets [year] when the report is organised by year (year locates the report); round brackets (year) when the report is organised by volume number (year is the year of decision). When a case has a neutral citation and is in a volume-organised report, the year appears in both.
types.validation: Year is four digits. Neutral citation, where present, precedes the reported citation and is separated by a comma. Volume number always Arabic.
types.pinpoint: Preceded by ' at '. Paragraphs in square brackets [x] (no 'para'/'paragraph'); pages plain (no 'p'). Subparagraph within brackets [238(a)]. Ranges: en dash (–) without spaces, not elided (92–98 not 92–8). Multiples: commas with final 'and' e.g. at [30], [40] and [47]. First page repeated if pinpoint is to first page. Footnote in a source: ', n x'.
types.subsequentForm: General style (2.3.1): first citation gives full details including case name even if named in text; thereafter if the source is obvious from context give only the pinpoint (e.g. 'At [52]'); if not obvious, repeat the case name then ', above n x,' + pinpoint (e.g. 'R v Wang, above n 49, at 533'). A reference tag may replace the case name (2.3.2). Do not use ibid. Commercial style: repeat full citation each time.
types.parseStructure: *Case name* [space] [optional neutral citation ','] [space] year(bracketed) [space] optional-volume [space] ReportSeries [space] StartingPage [space] optional-(Court) [' at ' pinpoint]. Delimiters: comma between neutral and reported citation; round brackets around court identifier; ' at ' before pinpoint.

examples.correct_citation: Z v Dental Complaints Assessment Committee [2008] NZSC 55, [2009] 1 NZLR 1 at [26].
Body Corporate 202254 v Taylor [2008] NZCA 317, [2009] 2 NZLR 17 at [76(c)].
Taylor v New Zealand Poultry Board [1984] 1 NZLR 394 (CA) at 398.
Hawkins v Minister of Justice [1991] 2 NZLR 530 (CA) at 534.
Commerce Commission v Progressive Enterprises Ltd [2010] NZCA 374, (2010) 12 TCLR 736 at [38].
Gray v Gray (1887) 5 NZLR CA 111.

types.name: Neutral-citation (unreported) case, New Zealand

components.label: Case name
components.formatting: as for reported cases (3.2.1); note in unreported cases 'The Queen' abbreviates to 'R'

components.label: Year
components.formatting: square brackets, exactly as on the judgment; this is the year the case was decided

components.label: Court identifier
components.omittedWhen: never (a separate court identifier after the page is NOT added — it is part of the neutral citation)
components.formatting: official identifier adopted by the court e.g. NZSC, NZCA, NZHC, NZDC, NZACC, NZEmpC, NZEnvC, NZFC, NZYC, UKPC; tribunals e.g. NZHRRT, NZLCDT; for NZERA/NZTT/NZWHT the district follows the identifier before the number

components.label: Judgment number
components.formatting: unique sequential number issued by the court

components.label: Pinpoint reference
components.formatting: as rule 3.2.8 (paragraphs in square brackets)

types.bracketRules: Year always in square brackets in a neutral citation.
types.validation: Neutral citation form is [year] COURT number. Year four digits. Only official neutral citations from the original judgment; do not use NZLII/AustLII/CanLII/BAILII numbers.
types.pinpoint: As reported cases: ' at ' + [paragraph] in square brackets, or page.
types.subsequentForm: As reported cases (2.3.1): pinpoint alone if obvious, else 'Case name, above n x, at [y]'; or reference tag + ', above n x,'.
types.parseStructure: *Case name* [space] [year] [space] COURT [space] number [' at ' pinpoint]. No court identifier in round brackets after the number; no report series.

examples.correct_citation: Attorney-General v X [2007] NZCA 388 at [70].
North Shore City Council v Attorney-General [2010] NZSC 125.
Erwood v Ministry of Social Development [2010] NZCA 619 at [35].
Craggy Range Vineyards Ltd v Campbell [2008] NZCA 96.
Griffin v Citibus Ltd [2011] NZERA Christchurch 137.

types.name: Unreported case (file number format), New Zealand

components.label: Case name
components.formatting: as 3.2.1; 'The Queen' becomes 'R'

components.label: Court abbreviation
components.includedWhen: included for courts/tribunals with multiple registries (e.g. HC, DC, FC)
components.omittedWhen: omit for single-registry courts (Supreme Court, Court of Appeal) — court is obvious from the file number
components.formatting: HC (High Court), DC (District Court), FC (Family Court); SC for pre-1980 Supreme Court; Appendix 1 for others

components.label: Registry
components.formatting: location written in full, no abbreviations

components.label: File number
components.formatting: current HC/DC/FC format CIV-year-XXX-XXXXXX / CRI-year-XXX-XXXXXX / FAM-year-XXX-XXXXXX (each part hyphen-separated, leading zeroes omitted, final part up to six digits); CA format CA[number]/[2-digit year] with no space; SC 2004 civil 'SC CIV n/2004', criminal 'SC CRI n/2004'; remove 'no'; no space between letters and numbers; if multiple file numbers give only the first

components.label: Date of judgment
components.formatting: preceded by a comma; month written in full; all four digits of the year; date judgment delivered (not date reasons given)

types.bracketRules: No year brackets; date is written out (day month year). A minute/ruling description may follow the date in round brackets, e.g. (Minute No 16).
types.validation: Comma between file number and date. No spaces within file numbers between letters and numbers.
types.subsequentForm: As reported cases (2.3.1): pinpoint if obvious, else 'Case name, above n x, at [y]', or reference tag.
types.parseStructure: *Case name* [space] [optional CourtAbbrev] [space] [optional Registry] [space] FileNumber ',' [space] Date [' at ' pinpoint].

examples.correct_citation: R v Reekie CA339/03, 3 August 2004 at [35].
R v Tuhou HC Napier CRI-2007-020-2820, 11 September 2008 at [13].
Plot Ltd v Brereton HC Christchurch CIV-2007-409-2659, 17 January 2008.
Chirnside v Fay SC CIV 7/2004, 26 August 2004.
Greenbaum v Waikato District Health Board ERA Auckland AA506/10, 10 December 2010.
Wellington International Airport Ltd v Commerce Commission HC Wellington CIV-2011-485-249, 1 June 2011 (Minute No 17) at [2].

components.omittedWhen: succession/no-subject-matter applications may substitute 'Estate of ...' or omit a specific block

components.label: Year of judgment
components.formatting: round brackets for all Māori Land Court decisions and pre-2010 Māori Appellate Court decisions; square brackets for post-2010 Māori Appellate Court and all Chief Judge's minute book decisions

components.label: Minute book reference

components.label: Citation (abbreviated)
components.formatting: round brackets; abbreviated minute-book citation e.g. (178 WAR 32), (2018 APPEAL 17), (2017 CJ 144); district abbreviations TTK, WMN, WAR, TRW, TKT, AOT, TWP, APPEAL, CJ

types.bracketRules: Year in round brackets for Māori Land Court and pre-2010 Māori Appellate Court; square brackets for post-2010 Māori Appellate Court and Chief Judge's minute book. Abbreviated citation always in round brackets at the end.
types.validation: En dash separates case name and block name. Abbreviated citation duplicates the minute book reference in short form.
types.parseStructure: *Case name* ' – ' BlockName [space] year(bracketed) [space] volume FullMinuteBookTitle MB folio [space] '(' shortCitation ')' [' at ' pinpoint].

types.name: New Zealand statute (Act, 1854 on)

components.label: Short title
components.formatting: exactly as in the statute book, in ordinary text (NOT italics); no full stops in abbreviations; if no short title use the unofficial short title from the bound reprints' contents, else the long title

components.label: Year enacted
components.formatting: year of enactment (not commencement)

components.label: Jurisdiction
components.includedWhen: included only when needed to distinguish a NZ Act from an overseas one; for overseas Acts an abbreviated jurisdiction in round brackets after the year
components.omittedWhen: OMIT for New Zealand statutes (do NOT write '(NZ)')
components.formatting: round brackets e.g. (UK), (Bermuda); write in full if no common abbreviation

components.label: Pinpoint reference
components.formatting: abbreviations s/ss, subs/subss, para/paras, sch/schs, pt/pts, art/arts, r/rr, reg/regs, cl/cls, etc. ('Section' spelt out if first word of a sentence); subsection within its own section cited as a section e.g. s 67(2); no comma between schedule and provision e.g. sch 3 cl 4; may be placed before the title as 'pinpoint of the ShortTitle'

types.bracketRules: Jurisdiction identifier (overseas only) in round brackets after the year. No brackets around the year.
types.validation: Year four digits. No '(NZ)' for New Zealand Acts. No full stops in abbreviations.
types.pinpoint: End position: preceded by a comma, e.g. ', s 59'. Start position: 'pinpoint of the ShortTitle year', e.g. 's 36 of the Commerce Act 1986'. Ranges use en dash e.g. s 24(f)–(g). Sub-provisions include the parent, e.g. s 50(1)(a)(i), unless clear from context. Schedule provision: 'sch 3 cl 4' (no comma).
types.subsequentForm: 2.3.1(a)(ii): if obvious from context give only the section (e.g. 'Section 8.'); if not obvious repeat the short title + comma + section but drop the year and jurisdiction unless needed to distinguish two Acts with the same short title. Commercial style: repeat full citation each time.
types.parseStructure: ShortTitle [space] Year [optional ' (' Jurisdiction ')'] [', ' pinpoint]. Pinpoint may alternatively lead: pinpoint ' of the ' ShortTitle Year.

Evidence Act 2006, s 44.

Property (Relationships) Act 1976, s 2 definition of “family chattels”, para (b).

types.bracketRules: Commas surround 'above n x'. Legislation drops year/jurisdiction; texts may add an abbreviated title.
types.validation: Never use 'ibid'. Two styles: GENERAL (student/academic/court/judgment work — uses 'above n x') and COMMERCIAL (publishers — repeat full citation for cases and legislation each time, but use the general style for texts/articles/essays). Confirm with the publisher which style applies.
types.pinpoint: If the source is obvious, give only the pinpoint ('At [52].'). Otherwise identifier + ', above n x,' + pinpoint. Where two successive footnotes cite the same source with no pinpoint, use 'Source, above n x.'
types.subsequentForm: This IS the subsequent-reference rule. Reference tags: give the tag + ', above n x,' (2.3.2); an obvious tag (a party's name) need not be introduced, a less obvious one (popular name) is introduced in square brackets at first citation.
types.parseStructure: [Identifier] [', above n ' x ','] [' at ' pinpoint]  — or just 'At ' pinpoint where the source is obvious.

examples.correct_citation: R v Wang, above n 49, at 533.

globalRules.quotationMarks: Double quotation marks are the default (rule 1.1.2). Double quotation marks enclose: short quotations (fewer than 30 words) within the text (1.2.2(a)(i)); titles of articles, essays/chapters in edited books (6.2.3), journal articles (6.4.3), internet documents (7.1.3), newspaper/magazine articles (7.2.3), press releases (7.4.3), speeches (7.5.3), tweets (7.1.10), submissions and many official-document titles; and words used in an unconventional way or referred to as words. Single quotation marks are used only for a quotation within a quotation (1.2.2(b)(i)) and for quotation marks appearing WITHIN a title that is itself in double quotes (6.4.3, 7.1.3, 7.2.3). The Guide's own examples use curly/typographic quotes “ ” and ‘ ’.
globalRules.italicsGeneral: Italicise: names of parties to cases including the 'v' (1.1.3, 3.2.1); names of newspapers (1.1.3, 7.2.4); titles of books/texts (1.1.3, 6.1.3) and government reports (1.1.3, 5.4(b)); foreign-language words/expressions not in current NZ usage (1.1.1(e)) and translations of text titles; case names/parties/phase in international decisions (10.2, 10.3); resolution and document titles in some international materials (10.4). Do NOT italicise: Māori and English words generally (1.1.3); Latin/French terms in common legal usage (1.1.1(d)); statute short titles (4.1.1(a)); treaty names (10.1.1(a)); article/essay/journal/newspaper/internet/press-release titles (these take double quotation marks); URLs (7.1.6). Emphasis is added by italicising, used sparingly (1.1.4). Reference tags take the formatting of the original name (1.1.7(c)).
globalRules.dates: Always write dates in the format '28 October 1965' (day month year, month in full, four-digit year) (1.2.3(b)). Month is written out in full without abbreviation throughout (e.g. case dates 3.4.6). Decades given in full without an apostrophe: '1990s' not '90s' or 'the nineties' (1.2.3(d)). Spans of years given in full: '1985–1987' not '1985–87' (1.2.3(d)).
globalRules.pinpointsGeneral: Pinpoints are introduced by ' at ' (e.g. 'at [26]', 'at 398'). A paragraph pinpoint is enclosed in SQUARE brackets [x] and no 'para'/'paragraph' word is used (3.2.8); square brackets are added even if the source does not bracket its paragraph numbers. Page numbers are given plain with no 'p'/'pp'/'page'. Subparagraph within brackets, e.g. [238(a)]. Multiple pinpoints: separate by commas with the final one preceded by 'and', e.g. 'at [30], [40] and [47]'. Ranges: separate by an en dash (–) with NO spaces and do NOT elide, e.g. '92–98' (not 92–8), '[153]–[162]'. Footnotes/endnotes within a source: 'at [page/para], n x' where x is the footnote number, e.g. 'at 189, n 92'. A single footnote covers both the case reference and its pinpoint (do not split them) (2.2.2). Where a pinpoint is to the first page, repeat that page number.
globalRules.multipleAuthors: Verbatim (6.1.2(e)): 'If there are two or three joint authors of a book, include the names of all authors, with the names of the last two authors separated by an “and”.' 'If there are more than three joint authors, note the name of the first-listed author followed by “and others”.' The same 2–3 / 4+ rule is applied to essays/chapters (6.2.4) and, by cross-reference, to reports, internet materials, newspaper articles, press releases, etc. (each cites author 'in accordance with rule 6.1.2').
globalRules.etAl: The Guide does not use the Latin 'et al'. Where there are more than three joint authors it uses 'and others' after the first-listed author's name (6.1.2(e)). In footnotes, abbreviated introductory signals such as 'et seq' are prohibited; use '… and following' instead (2.2.4(b)). ('et al' is not adopted; the equivalent is 'and others'.)
globalRules.footnotePunctuation: Verbatim (2.2.4(a)): 'Begin each footnote with an initial capital letter and conclude with a full stop.' 'Where several sources are cited for one proposition in a footnote, separate them by semicolons. The final source should be preceded by “and”.' 'Only use punctuation where it is grammatically necessary and not to indicate abbreviation.' Example: '45 Edwards v O’Connor [1991] 2 NZLR 543 (CA); L G Thorne & Co v Thomas Borthwick & Sons [1956] SR (NSW) 81 (SC); and State Rail Authority v Heath Outdoor Ltd (1986) 7 NSWLR 170 (CA).' Footnote numbers are superscript in the text, not bracketed, not followed by a full stop, and run consecutively through the work (2.2.1); a footnote number at the end of a sentence follows the full stop, at the end of a clause it follows the comma (2.2.2).
globalRules.subsequentReferences: Verbatim guidance (2.3.1(a)): 'The first time a source is cited, provide full citation details. For subsequent references there are two general rules: (1) If the source being referred to is obvious from the context, it is sufficient simply to refer to the relevant pinpoint reference. (2) If the source being referred to is not obvious from the context, give an “, above n x,” cross-reference. Use this method for subsequent references instead of using ibid.' The Guide does NOT use ibid or idem; it uses 'above n x' (with surrounding commas). Reference tags may replace a repeated case name (2.3.2). Two overall styles exist: the GENERAL style (student, academic, court submissions, judgments) and the COMMERCIAL style used by some publishers (repeat full citation details for cases and legislation each time, no reference tags, but use the general style for texts/articles/essays). Where two successive footnotes cite the same source without a pinpoint, use '“, above n x,”' (e.g. 'Rainy Sky SA v Kookmin Bank, above n 10.').
globalRules.abbreviations: Verbatim (1.1.2 / 2.1.3): 'Only punctuate when grammatically necessary, and not to indicate abbreviation.' Hence 'Kós P' NOT 'Kós P.'; 'CA' NOT 'C.A.'; 'ADLS' NOT 'A.D.L.S.'; 'NATO' with no full stops or spaces. Full stops indicating abbreviation are removed even inside quotations and case/title names. When a full stop is removed from an abbreviation of more than a single letter, a space is generally left where the full stop was (2.1.3). Do not use the Oxford/serial comma except where it provides clarity (1.1.2). Do not use 'etc' or abbreviated signals 'cf', 'f', 'ff', 'et seq' (1.1.7(a), 2.2.4(b)).
globalRules.jurisdictionIdentifiers: Cases: generally unnecessary because the jurisdiction is obvious from the report series or neutral citation; add a jurisdiction tag before the court identifier (no space) when citing from a multijurisdictional report series (e.g. (NZCA), (NZHC), (Fiji HC)) (3.2.7(c)); with an official neutral citation the identifier already encodes the jurisdiction and no separate court identifier is added (3.2.7(a)). Legislation: for NEW ZEALAND statutes do NOT add '(NZ)' (4.1.1(c)); for overseas statutes add an abbreviated jurisdiction in round brackets after the year, or write it in full where there is no common abbreviation. Australian statute identifiers (Cth, ACT, NSW, NT, Qld, SA, Tas, Vic, WA, 9.2) DIFFER from Australian case-report jurisdiction identifiers (ACT, NSW, NT, Q, SA, TAS, V, WA, 8.2.2). UK pre-1963 statutes use Eng/GB/UK/Imp (9.4.1(c)); UK Parliament modern Acts add '(UK)', but Scottish/Welsh/NI Acts carry the jurisdiction in the title and take no identifier (9.4.3). In a bibliography, country identifiers are NOT included (Appendix 7 V). Country names are generally not abbreviated; 'New Zealand' is never abbreviated to 'NZ', 'United Kingdom' not 'UK', 'United States' not 'USA' (1.1.7(d)) — except as a jurisdiction tag attached to a court identifier.
